title: Message-scaffold compatibility shim and onboarding validation for subword mapping
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: New community models use subtle differences in message framing (role markers, whitespace anchors, and subword escape policies) that cause runtime prefixing, KV-cache hits, and published performance profiles to diverge during onboarding. This leads to: 1) skewed token counts vs. published profiles, 2) degraded latency when the runtime falls back to conservative batching, and 3) wrong fallback pins when a version alias mismatch occurs.

Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility shim (message-scaffold shim) plus an onboarding validation harness that detects mapping mismatches between model tokenizer behavior and Redwood chat templates, produces actionable diffs, and optionally applies a non-destructive alignment shim before pinning a model version or publishing its performance profile. The shim must be reversible and observable so we don't mask upstream model issues.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding harness can detect subword-splitting and role-delimiter differences between the model tokenizer and Redwood chat templates with a deterministic test corpus
Compatibility shim that translates inbound message scaffolds (role delimiters, ephemeral whitespace markers) to the model-native framing is implemented as an opt-in runtime layer
Published performance profiles reflect token counts post-shim; a pre-shim vs post-shim diff is recorded in the profile metadata
Pinning workflow requires an explicit acknowledgement when a shim is applied to a pinned version
Automated tests cover KV-cache invariants (cache hit rates do not regress by >2% after shim) and latency SLOs under representative batching
Design doc and PR with benchmarks, and an E2E demo runbook are linked in the ticket
steps: Create a small deterministic test corpus representing common chat patterns, edge case role markers, and long prefix contexts
Add tokenizer-probing harness that runs tokenization with the model binary and with Redwood canonical serializer to build a diff map
Prototype a reversible compatibility shim that rewrites message scaffolds to model-native form at the runtime ingress (configurable via model profile)
Integrate shim-flag into onboarding UI/CLI so PM/DS can preview pre/post tokenization counts and accept shim before pinning
Run microbenchmarks comparing latency, throughput, and KV-cache hit rate with and without shim on dedicated test pool
Publish updated performance profile schema fields: shim_applied, shim_diff_summary, pre_tokens, post_tokens
Ship unit/integration tests and a small migration script to annotate recent onboarded profiles that used manual shimning
mitigation_plan: If shim causes unexpected regressions in production test customers, flip an opt-out flag per-customer and auto-roll back to pre-shim behavior. Telemetry will emit shim_breaking=true alerts and include recent prompt samples to aid triage.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ava Chen: Spike complete. Initial corpus of 120 prompt variants created; found 3 common delimiter patterns across 6 community models that change leading token counts by 1-4 tokens per prompt.
2025-02-20 - Ravi Patel: Prototype shim implemented in ingress; basic reversible rewrite for role markers works for 4/6 models. Need to handle zero-width-space variants and surrogate unicode markers.

2025-02-26 - PM review (Marisol Ortega): PM asks that any applied shim be surfaced in the Console onboarding flow and that release notes include guidance for customers. Added UI task to product backlog.
2025-03-01 - Performance (Jinsoo Park): Microbenchmarks show 1.8% KV-cache hit rate improvement post-shim on chat-heavy workload; end-to-end median latency unchanged within noise.
2025-03-03 - Security (Elena Ruiz): Reviewed shim for injection risk; recommend escaping rules for message rewriting and KMS audit of profile changes. No blocking issues.
2025-03-04 - Ravi Patel: Working on tests to ensure shim metadata is included when publishing profile; preparing PR and benchmark artifacts. Planning canary rollout to internal customers next week.
